boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Santa Clara University
boards.description: Ten currently documented late-hour destinations in and around Santa Clara University, with access details kept conservative.

cards.title: University Library
cards.subtitle: Santa Clara University campus
cards.notes: Use the library’s posted standard-hours schedule to plan a study stop; confirm exceptions for breaks or exam periods before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A campus study destination with standard Monday–Thursday and Sunday hours extending to 2 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Santa Clara University lists standard library hours of 7 a.m.–2 a.m. Monday–Thursday and 9 a.m.–2 a.m. Sunday, with changes possible during breaks and exams.
cards.source_title: Students — Santa Clara University
cards.access_notes: Standard hours listed: Monday–Thursday 7 a.m.–2 a.m.; Sunday 9 a.m.–2 a.m. Hours may change during exam periods and breaks.

cards.entity_name: Pat Malley Fitness and Recreation Center
cards.title: Pat Malley Fitness and Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: Santa Clara University campus
cards.notes: Check the recreation center’s schedule before an evening workout and allow time to wrap up before the posted midnight closing window.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation facility whose listed Monday–Thursday and Sunday hours run until midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Santa Clara University lists Malley Recreation Center hours until midnight Monday–Thursday and Sunday.
cards.source_title: Students — Santa Clara University
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: Monday–Thursday 6:30 a.m.–midnight and Sunday 10 a.m.–midnight; verify changes before visiting.

cards.title: The Bronco
cards.subtitle: Benson Center, Santa Clara University
cards.notes: Look for Benson Center late-night programming if you want a campus gathering place with food and games; event offerings can vary.
cards.short_summary: The university identifies this Benson Center venue within its late-night food and entertainment programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Santa Clara University’s Late Night Programs page identifies The Bronco and describes late-night food, entertainment, free billiards, and foosball without a cover charge.
cards.source_title: Late Night Programs — Benson Center — Santa Clara University
cards.access_notes: SCU designates this as late-night programming; check the Benson Center page for the current program schedule before going.

cards.entity_name: Dae Bak Korean Fusion Eatery & Lounge
cards.title: Dae Bak Korean Fusion Eatery & Lounge
cards.subtitle: 3284 El Camino Real, Santa Clara
cards.notes: For a very late food stop, use the restaurant’s own ordering information and place an online order before its stated ordering cutoff.
cards.short_summary: A Santa Clara Korean-fusion restaurant that says it remains open until 2 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Dae Bak’s official website states that it is open until 2 a.m. and that online orders close at 11:30 p.m.
cards.source_title: Dae Bak Korean Fusion Eatery & Lounge
cards.access_notes: The business states it is open until 2 a.m.; online orders close at 11:30 p.m. Verify service details before travel.

cards.title: Giiwa
cards.subtitle: 1494 Halford Avenue, Santa Clara
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s listed daily closing time as a late-evening checkpoint, and confirm seating or pickup availability directly before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A Santa Clara restaurant whose official site lists daily hours through 11:30 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Giiwa’s official website lists daily operating hours of 10 a.m. to 11:30 p.m. at 1494 Halford Avenue in Santa Clara.
cards.source_title: About — Giiwa Santa Clara
cards.access_notes: Officially listed as open daily 10 a.m.–11:30 p.m.; confirm current kitchen, dine-in, and pickup availability before visiting.

cards.title: Taco Bell on The Alameda
cards.subtitle: 2555 The Alameda, Santa Clara
cards.notes: This location’s drive-through is the late-hours option; check the separate dine-in and drive-through schedules before setting out.
cards.short_summary: A The Alameda location with drive-through hours listed until 2 a.m. most nights and 3 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-through hours until 2 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and until 3 a.m. Friday–Saturday at 2555 The Alameda.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell — 2555 The Alameda, Santa Clara
cards.access_notes: Drive-through: until 2 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 3 a.m. Friday–Saturday. Listed dine-in hours end earlier, at 10 p.m.

cards.title: Taco Bell on El Camino Real
cards.subtitle: 1680 El Camino Real, Santa Clara
cards.notes: Use this El Camino Real location when drive-through access suits the plan; its posted dine-in hours end earlier than late service.
cards.short_summary: A Santa Clara drive-through location with posted service until 1 a.m. on weekdays and 3 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-through hours until 1 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 3 a.m. Friday–Saturday at 1680 El Camino Real.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell — 1680 El Camino Real, Santa Clara
cards.access_notes: Drive-through: until 1 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 3 a.m. Friday–Saturday. Listed dine-in hours end at 9 p.m.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Homestead Road
cards.subtitle: 2600 Homestead Road, Santa Clara
cards.notes: Treat the drive-through schedule as the late option here, and check the location page for any same-day changes before the trip.
cards.short_summary: A Santa Clara drive-through location with posted late service until 2 a.m. most nights and 3:45 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-through hours until 2 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and until 3:45 a.m. Friday–Saturday at 2600 Homestead Road.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell — 2600 Homestead Road, Santa Clara
cards.access_notes: Drive-through: until 2 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 3:45 a.m. Friday–Saturday. Listed dine-in hours end at 10 p.m.

cards.title: Denny’s on El Camino Real
cards.subtitle: 1745 El Camino Real, Santa Clara
cards.notes: For an all-hours food stop, use the restaurant’s official location page and contact the location if you need holiday-specific confirmation.
cards.short_summary: A Santa Clara Denny’s location whose official page lists restaurant hours as open 24 hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Denny’s lists its restaurant at 1745 El Camino Real in Santa Clara as open 24 hours.
cards.source_title: Denny’s — 1745 El Camino Real, Santa Clara
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists restaurant hours as open 24 hours and advises contacting the restaurant to confirm holiday hours.

cards.entity_name: Jack in the Box — 3465 Homestead Road
cards.title: Jack in the Box on Homestead Road
cards.subtitle: 3465 Homestead Road, Santa Clara
cards.notes: Plan around the drive-through schedule rather than lobby hours, which the official location page lists as ending earlier in the evening.
cards.short_summary: A Homestead Road drive-through with posted service to 2 a.m. most nights and 3 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Jack in the Box lists drive-through hours at 3465 Homestead Road until 2 a.m. most nights and 3 a.m. Thursday through Saturday.
cards.source_title: Jack in the Box — 3465 Homestead Road, Santa Clara
cards.access_notes: Drive-through is listed until 2 a.m. most nights and 3 a.m. Thursday–Saturday; the lobby is listed until 10 p.m.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other

cards.title: Harrington Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: University Library
cards.notes: Use the library’s learning commons for individual work, group work, research help, or a planned study session between classes.
cards.short_summary: A library-based setting for solo and collaborative academic work.
cards.evidence_claim: Santa Clara University Library identifies the Harrington Learning Commons as part of its student learning environment.
cards.source_title: Library Building | Santa Clara University Library
cards.access_notes: Confirm building access and service availability with the library before visiting.

cards.title: Benson Memorial Center
cards.subtitle: Campus dining and student gathering destination
cards.notes: Meet a classmate in the student center, then use its listed dining and campus-service areas as a convenient starting point.
cards.short_summary: A central student-center stop with dining and services.
cards.evidence_claim: Santa Clara University lists Benson Memorial Center on its campus map and identifies it as a campus facility.
cards.source_title: Santa Clara University Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Food and retail purchases may be required depending on the activity.

cards.title: Mission Santa Clara de Asís
cards.subtitle: Historic mission church on the SCU campus
cards.notes: Pause to view the mission’s architecture and history, then check posted guidance before entering or attending a scheduled service.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus landmark with an active religious role.
cards.evidence_claim: Santa Clara University identifies Mission Santa Clara de Asís as a campus destination and describes its mission history.
cards.source_title: Mission Santa Clara de Asís | Santa Clara University
cards.access_notes: Observe any service, visitor, and photography guidance posted by the Mission.

cards.title: Mission Gardens
cards.subtitle: Mission Santa Clara de Asís grounds
cards.notes: Build in a quiet outdoor pause while walking the historic mission grounds; stay on open paths and follow any event signage.
cards.short_summary: Historic mission grounds suited to a reflective campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Santa Clara University lists Mission Gardens as a named location on its campus map.
cards.source_title: Santa Clara University Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access can change for services, university events, or maintenance.

cards.title: Adobe Lodge
cards.subtitle: Office of Student Life location
cards.notes: Use the named Student Life location as a practical waypoint when seeking involvement information, student support, or campus-program guidance.
cards.short_summary: A campus destination associated with student-life support.
cards.evidence_claim: Santa Clara University lists Adobe Lodge as the location of the Office of Student Life.
cards.source_title: Contact Us | Office of Student Life | Santa Clara University
cards.access_notes: Office services and visitor availability depend on posted business hours.

cards.title: Locatelli Student Activity Center
cards.subtitle: Student activity and recreation facility
cards.notes: Check the facility schedule for open recreation or student programs, and bring any required campus identification for entry.
cards.short_summary: A named campus recreation and student-activity facility.
cards.evidence_claim: Santa Clara University lists the Locatelli Student Activity Center on its campus map.
cards.source_title: Santa Clara University Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Access, programs, and equipment availability may vary by schedule.

cards.title: Malley Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: Campus fitness facility
cards.notes: Plan a workout or fitness class by reviewing recreation information first, then follow current entry and equipment-use requirements.
cards.short_summary: A campus destination for fitness and recreation activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Santa Clara University Recreation identifies Malley Fitness Center as a campus fitness facility.
cards.source_title: Malley Fitness Center | Santa Clara University Recreation
cards.access_notes: Review current recreation policies, hours, and eligibility before arrival.

cards.entity_name: Sobrato Campus for Discovery and Innovation
cards.title: Sobrato Campus for Discovery and Innovation
cards.subtitle: Academic and innovation complex
cards.notes: Walk through the named academic complex while heading to a class, event, or department appointment, respecting room access signs.
cards.short_summary: A modern academic complex supporting university teaching and innovation.
cards.evidence_claim: Santa Clara University identifies the Sobrato Campus for Discovery and Innovation as a campus academic facility.
cards.source_title: Sobrato Campus for Discovery and Innovation | Santa Clara University
cards.access_notes: Some classrooms, labs, and event areas may have restricted access.

cards.title: de Saisset Museum
cards.subtitle: Santa Clara University art museum
cards.notes: Visit an exhibition or use the museum as a cultural stop between campus commitments; review current visitor information before going.
cards.short_summary: A campus art museum with rotating exhibitions and collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Santa Clara University’s de Saisset Museum provides exhibitions and collection-based programming on campus.
cards.source_title: de Saisset Museum | Santa Clara University
cards.access_notes: Check current exhibition dates and visitor guidance before your visit.

cards.title: St. Clare Room
cards.subtitle: Benson Memorial Center
cards.notes: Use this named Benson destination when meeting for a scheduled campus event, presentation, or organization gathering; confirm the room booking first.
cards.short_summary: A named room within the campus student center.
cards.evidence_claim: Santa Clara University lists the St. Clare Room as a named location in Benson Memorial Center.
cards.source_title: Santa Clara University Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Room access is event- and reservation-dependent.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Santa Clara University study environments, from computer-ready commons to reservable collaborative rooms.

cards.title: Lower Information Commons
cards.subtitle: Learning Commons lower level
cards.notes: Set up near the lower-level desktop stations when you need campus software alongside individual study time and a nearby printer.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level computer study area with Windows and iMac stations.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU identifies the Lower Information Commons on the Learning Commons lower level and lists Windows Dell desktops and iMacs for student use there.
cards.source_title: Learning Commons' Computing and Media Facilities
cards.access_notes: Located on the lower level of the Learning Commons; campus computer use is described for students.

cards.title: Upper Information Commons
cards.subtitle: Learning Commons first floor
cards.notes: Use the first-floor public computers for a focused work block, especially when you need Windows tools, macOS, or SmartPrint nearby.
cards.short_summary: First-floor desktop stations in the Learning Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU states that the Upper Information Commons is on the first floor and has a mix of Windows-based Dell desktops and iMacs available for student use.
cards.source_title: Learning Commons' Computing and Media Facilities
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor; SCU describes the computers as available for student use.

cards.title: Learning Commons 203
cards.subtitle: Second-floor training and instructional lab
cards.notes: Check whether instruction is scheduled, then use an open workstation for coursework that benefits from installed lab software and campus hardware.
cards.short_summary: A 30-workstation lab that becomes a drop-in lab when unscheduled.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU lists Learning Commons 203 as a 30-workstation training and instructional room that is available as a drop-in lab when not scheduled.
cards.source_title: Learning Commons' Computing and Media Facilities
cards.access_notes: Drop-in use is available only when the room is not scheduled for instruction.

cards.title: Learning Commons 205
cards.subtitle: Second-floor training and instructional lab
cards.notes: Bring a project that needs a full computer lab and use this room during unscheduled periods; ask Technology Training about reservations if needed.
cards.short_summary: A 50-workstation Learning Commons computer lab.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU identifies Learning Commons 205 as a 50-workstation training and instructional room and says unscheduled instructional labs are open for regular computer use.
cards.source_title: Technology Training Locations
cards.access_notes: Use for regular computer work when not in instruction; SCU says the labs follow regular building hours.

cards.title: Learning Commons 206
cards.subtitle: Second-floor training and instructional lab
cards.notes: Choose this lab for computer-based coursework when it is not reserved for instruction, and plan around the Learning Commons’ regular building hours.
cards.short_summary: A 20-workstation training lab that can operate as drop-in space.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU lists Learning Commons 206 as a 20-workstation instructional room and says these rooms are available as drop-in labs when not scheduled.
cards.source_title: Learning Commons' Computing and Media Facilities
cards.access_notes: Drop-in availability depends on the instructional schedule.

cards.title: Learning Commons 331
cards.subtitle: Third-floor Multimedia Lab
cards.notes: Use the third-floor multimedia lab when you need an available lab computer; confirm that no instructional session is occupying the room first.
cards.short_summary: A named third-floor lab for regular computer use between classes.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU lists Learning Commons 331 among its training and instructional labs and says those labs are open for regular computer use when not in instruction.
cards.source_title: Technology Training Locations
cards.access_notes: Located on the third floor; availability is limited to times the room is not used for instruction and regular building hours.

cards.title: Learning Commons Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Reservable collaborative rooms
cards.notes: Reserve with your SCU ID for a group session, then check in on the door tablet within ten minutes or the reservation can be released.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms with a whiteboard, table, chairs, and display connection.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU says its group study rooms are for the SCU community, reservable with an SCU ID, and equipped with tables, 6–8 chairs, whiteboards, and device-connectable screens.
cards.source_title: Group Study Rooms
cards.access_notes: SCU community only; reserve with SCU ID up to seven days ahead for up to four hours daily, or claim an available room in person.

cards.title: Viewing and Production A
cards.subtitle: Learning Commons 129
cards.notes: Reserve this 58-seat media room when a team needs a supported setting for a presentation rehearsal, screening, web conference, or recording.
cards.short_summary: A reservable 58-seat room equipped for media-based project work.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU identifies Viewing and Production A as Learning Commons 129, with 58 seats, and says it supports recordings, screenings, web conferences, and webinars by reservation.
cards.source_title: Learning Commons' Computing and Media Facilities
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required; SCU directs users to contact Media Services to reserve the room.

cards.title: Lucas Hall
cards.subtitle: Leavey School of Business shared study spaces
cards.notes: Use the room-reservation system when your group needs a shared study space in Lucas Hall, then plan your meeting around the confirmed booking.
cards.short_summary: A business-school building with study spaces and reservable shared study space.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU states that Lucas Hall houses study spaces, and its student technology guide lists Lucas Hall among locations with shared study spaces reservable through Room Reservation.
cards.source_title: Quick Start Guide for Students
cards.access_notes: Shared study spaces are reserved through the Room Reservation service using the MySCU Portal.

cards.entity_name: Howard S. and Alida S. Charney Hall of Law
cards.title: Charney Hall of Law
cards.subtitle: Shared study spaces in Charney Hall
cards.notes: Book a shared study space through MySCU before heading to Charney Hall, especially for a focused meeting that needs a defined academic setting.
cards.short_summary: A law-school building with reservable shared study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU’s student technology guide lists Charney Hall among the locations with shared study spaces that can be reserved through Room Reservation.
cards.source_title: Quick Start Guide for Students
cards.access_notes: Shared study spaces are reserved through the Room Reservation service using the MySCU Portal.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: A corridor-by-corridor set of named destinations in the walkable campus-to-downtown area, each with a directly sourced reason to stop.

cards.title: Bagels across El Camino Real
cards.subtitle: El Camino Real corridor, opposite SCU’s main entrance
cards.notes: Cross to 495 El Camino Real for the bakery’s own bagel, breakfast-bagel, sandwich, smoothie, and lunch menu; check its site before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A directly opposite-campus stop with a broad bagel and sandwich menu.
cards.evidence_claim: Cramer's Bagels lists its Santa Clara address as 495 El Camino Real and offers bagels, breakfast bagels, bagel sandwiches, smoothies, and more.
cards.source_title: Cramer's Bagels
cards.access_notes: Business hours and menu availability are published by the business; confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Mission history on El Camino Real
cards.subtitle: El Camino Real corridor at SCU’s western edge
cards.notes: Use the Mission’s official history page to orient yourself before viewing the church from the El Camino Real side of the campus corridor.
cards.short_summary: The university’s documented historic Mission anchors the El Camino Real edge.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU identifies Mission Santa Clara de Asís as the eighth mission site in California and says the current church was built in 1927–28.
cards.source_title: Mission Church — SCU Campus Map
cards.access_notes: This destination is at the campus edge; respect church services and any posted access guidance.

cards.title: Portuguese pastry on El Camino Real
cards.subtitle: El Camino Real corridor, east of SCU
cards.notes: Head to 1085 El Camino Real if you want a pastry-stop option; the city’s visitor bureau specifically identifies the shop and its pastel de nata.
cards.short_summary: A named El Camino Real bakery documented for Portuguese pastries.
cards.evidence_claim: Discover Santa Clara lists Portuguese Tasty Desserts at 1085 El Camino Real and describes its pastel de nata as a Portuguese custard tart.
cards.source_title: Santa Clara Global Games Food Trail
cards.access_notes: Food and drinks require purchase; verify current business hours directly before going.

cards.title: Thai menu in Franklin Mall
cards.subtitle: Franklin Mall corridor, near Mission Branch Library
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s online menu to plan a carryout or dine-in meal at 1211 Franklin Mall; vegetarian options are listed among its food types.
cards.short_summary: A Franklin Mall restaurant with an official menu and vegetarian options.
cards.evidence_claim: Jasmine Thai Cuisine lists its location as 1211 Franklin Mall and identifies Thai dishes and vegetarian options on its official ordering site.
cards.source_title: Jasmine Thai Cuisine
cards.access_notes: The business posts separate dining, carryout, and delivery hours; check before visiting.

cards.title: Fountain at Franklin Square
cards.subtitle: Franklin Mall corridor at Monroe Street and Franklin Street
cards.notes: Pause at the Old Town Quad fountain while moving through Franklin Square; the city describes it as a waiting place for nearby bus passengers.
cards.short_summary: A city-listed fountain in the Old Town Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Santa Clara places Franklin Square Fountain at Monroe Street and Franklin Street and describes it as surrounded by small fountains in the Old Town Quad.
cards.source_title: Franklin Square Fountain — City of Santa Clara
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public artwork; follow any on-site rules and street-event closures.

cards.title: Public art at 1200 Franklin Mall
cards.subtitle: Franklin Mall corridor, Franklin Square area
cards.notes: Add this named city-listed artwork to a Franklin Mall walk, and consult the city’s public-art map for its recorded address and nearby works.
cards.short_summary: A distinct public-art stop in the Franklin Mall corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Santa Clara’s Art & Statues map lists the artwork Indians and Pioneers at 1200 Franklin Mall, Santa Clara.
cards.source_title: Art & Statues — City of Santa Clara
cards.access_notes: Outdoor artwork; view from public areas and observe any posted rules.

cards.title: Market at Jackson and Homestead
cards.subtitle: Jackson Street–Homestead Road corridor, downtown edge
cards.notes: Plan a Saturday morning loop around the market corner at Jackson Street and Homestead Road; confirm the specific date in the city calendar first.
cards.short_summary: A city-calendar market stop at a named downtown corner.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Santa Clara calendar locates the Santa Clara Farmers Market at the corner of Jackson Street and Homestead Road and lists a 9 a.m.–1 p.m. event time.
cards.source_title: Santa Clara Farmers Market — City of Santa Clara
cards.access_notes: The cited calendar occurrence is dated; check the current city calendar for market dates and vendor participation.

cards.title: Ice-cream tacos on Park Avenue
cards.subtitle: Park Avenue corridor beside The Alameda near SCU
cards.notes: Walk the Park Avenue block near The Alameda for a dessert stop; the official visitor guide identifies the shop’s waffle-cone taco shells and address.
cards.short_summary: A named Park Avenue dessert shop documented by the city visitor bureau.
cards.evidence_claim: Discover Santa Clara lists Rocko’s Ice Cream Tacos at 2905 Park Avenue and describes waffle-cone taco shells filled with ice cream.
cards.source_title: Santa Clara Global Games Food Trail
cards.access_notes: Food requires purchase; consult the business directly for current operating hours.

cards.entity_name: Voyager Craft Coffee — Alameda Santa Clara
cards.title: Coffee on The Alameda
cards.subtitle: The Alameda corridor, northwest of campus
cards.notes: Use Voyager’s location page to find its Alameda Santa Clara shop at 2221 The Alameda, then verify operating status and hours before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A named coffee location on The Alameda with published daily hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Voyager Craft Coffee lists its Alameda Santa Clara location at 2221 The Alameda and publishes daily 7 a.m.–5 p.m. hours.
cards.source_title: Voyager Craft Coffee Locations
cards.access_notes: The business’s location page lists daily hours; verify current operating status before going.

cards.title: Downtown blocks at Franklin Square
cards.subtitle: Franklin Street–Benton Street–Monroe Street–Jackson Street corridor
cards.notes: Use Franklin Square as the connective stop for a downtown walk; the city identifies its surrounding streets and describes its city-owned parking areas.
cards.short_summary: A named downtown complex bounded by four documented streets.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Santa Clara identifies Franklin Square parking lots as adjacent to Benton, Monroe, Jackson, and Homestead Road, and says the complex is maintained by the Downtown Parking Maintenance District.
cards.source_title: Franklin Square Paid Parking Project — City of Santa Clara
cards.access_notes: This is a public downtown complex; parking policies and event conditions may change.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Santa Clara rituals, songs, mascots, and recurring community gatherings rooted in Bronco campus life.

cards.title: Sing the SCU Fight Song
cards.subtitle: Bronco spirit tradition
cards.notes: Learn the official fight song before a campus gathering, then join in when the familiar red-and-white refrain starts.
cards.short_summary: Santa Clara preserves its fight song as a shared piece of Bronco spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU Alumni identifies the SCU Fight Song and Alma Mater as campus-life traditions and provides the song for listeners.
cards.source_title: History & Traditions - Alumni - Santa Clara University
cards.access_notes: Listen or view materials through the Alumni history-and-traditions page.

cards.title: Keep the Alma Mater Handy
cards.subtitle: Bronco ceremonial song
cards.notes: Read the official Alma Mater alongside the fight song so you can recognize Santa Clara’s two distinct school-song traditions.
cards.short_summary: The Alma Mater is preserved with Santa Clara’s official fight-song materials.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU Alumni states that the Alma Mater and Fight Song are distinct Santa Clara traditions.
cards.source_title: Rally Song Contest - Alumni - Santa Clara University
cards.access_notes: The Alumni page explains the Alma Mater’s distinct role from the Fight Song.

cards.title: Spot Bucky the Bronco
cards.subtitle: Athletics and campus-events mascot tradition
cards.notes: Bring a camera to an athletics matchup or university event; Bucky’s costumed appearance is a long-running visible Bronco ritual.
cards.short_summary: A mystery wearer has kept Santa Clara’s horse mascot tradition alive since 1976.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU reports that the Bucky mascot tradition dates to a 1976 makeshift Benny the Bronco costume; Benny became Bucky in 1995.
cards.source_title: The unbridled potential of Bucky the Bronco - Santa Clara University
cards.access_notes: Bucky appears at athletic matchups, university events, and community gatherings.

cards.title: Bagels & Greenbooks
cards.subtitle: Bannan Alumni House during Welcome to Finals
cards.notes: During Welcome to Finals week, stop at Bannan Alumni House for this quarterly study-season tradition and its bagel-and-greenbook handout.
cards.short_summary: A quarterly finals-week stop connecting current students with the Alumni Association.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU Alumni describes Bagels & Greenbooks as a quarterly tradition during Welcome to Finals week at Bannan Alumni House.
cards.source_title: Current Students - Alumni - Santa Clara University
cards.access_notes: Offered during Welcome to Finals week; consult Alumni programming for each quarter’s details.

cards.title: The Alumni Family BBQ
cards.subtitle: Welcome Weekend legacy-family gathering
cards.notes: If you are a legacy student, attend during Welcome Weekend to meet classmates and families with their own Santa Clara connections.
cards.short_summary: A Welcome Weekend gathering specifically for legacy students and their families.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU Alumni describes the Alumni Family BBQ as an opportunity for legacy students and families to meet classmates with strong University ties during Welcome Weekend.
cards.source_title: Current Students - Alumni - Santa Clara University
cards.access_notes: Intended for legacy students and their families during Welcome Weekend.

cards.title: Summer Send-Offs
cards.subtitle: Incoming-student and alumni tradition
cards.notes: Before your first term, look for a local send-off reception to meet incoming classmates alongside current students and alumni.
cards.short_summary: Alumni-hosted summer receptions welcome new Broncos before they arrive on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU Alumni calls Summer Send-Offs an annual SCU tradition, with receptions for incoming first-year and transfer students and parents.
cards.source_title: Current Students - Alumni - Santa Clara University
cards.access_notes: Held in summer in locations across the country; availability varies by area.

cards.title: Camino de los Muertos
cards.subtitle: SCU Día de los Muertos celebration
cards.notes: Walk the altar tour, enjoy the cultural programming, and take part respectfully in SCU’s Día de los Muertos community celebration.
cards.short_summary: A campus Día de los Muertos event created through a Santa Clara community partnership.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU says Camino de los Muertos began in November 2023 and is a collaboration among SCU, the Mexican Consulate of San Jose, and Univision 14.
cards.source_title: Camino de los Muertos - Santa Clara University
cards.access_notes: The official page lists the next event as October 31, 2026, with timing marked tentative.

cards.title: SCU PowWow
cards.subtitle: Annual Indigenous community gathering
cards.notes: Follow the Indigenous Legacy page for the next PowWow, and participate as a respectful guest in this campus community gathering.
cards.short_summary: A recurring SCU event connected to the University’s ongoing Indigenous initiatives.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU’s Indigenous Legacy page lists the SCU PowWow and identifies May 2, 2026 as its sixth anniversary.
cards.source_title: Understanding Santa Clara University and its Indigenous Legacy
cards.access_notes: Check the Indigenous Legacy page for future event information and participation guidance.

cards.title: Grand Reunion
cards.subtitle: Annual alumni homecoming tradition
cards.notes: If you are returning as an alum, plan around the published October dates and reconnect through Santa Clara’s designated reunion weekend.
cards.short_summary: A high-impact annual campus weekend for bringing Bronco alumni back together.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU’s Event Planning Office lists Grand Reunion as an annual high-impact event, scheduled for October 8–11, 2026 and October 7–10, 2027.
cards.source_title: University Event Planning Office - Santa Clara University
cards.access_notes: Published dates: October 8–11, 2026; October 7–10, 2027.

cards.title: Commencement in Bronco Red
cards.subtitle: Annual graduation ceremony tradition
cards.notes: For graduating seniors and guests, use the official commencement information to follow the annual ceremony and its Santa Clara academic pageantry.
cards.short_summary: Santa Clara marks each graduating class with an annual commencement celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU reported that its 2026 ceremony was the University’s 175th commencement, and its event calendar lists future undergraduate and graduate commencement weekends.
cards.source_title: Santa Clara University’s largest-ever graduating class celebrates commencement
cards.access_notes: SCU’s event calendar lists Undergraduate and Graduate Commencement Weekend for June 12–13, 2026.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Santa Clara University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, on-campus sequence of historic, cultural, study, nature, and recreation stops for getting oriented.

cards.title: Begin at the Mission Church
cards.subtitle: Historic center of campus
cards.notes: Walk through the Mission Church early in the weekend and use the virtual tour or campus-history materials to orient yourself before exploring nearby paths.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus landmark with a daily visitor window.
cards.evidence_claim: Mission Santa Clara de Asís sits at the heart of SCU’s campus and invites visitors every day from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.
cards.source_title: Mission Santa Clara de Asís
cards.access_notes: Visitors are invited daily, 7 a.m.–7 p.m.; worship services follow the academic schedule.

cards.title: Circle through the Mission Gardens
cards.subtitle: Beside Mission Santa Clara de Asís
cards.notes: Continue outside after the church visit, following the garden paths and looking for the adobe wall and Adobe Lodge described on the museum’s walking-tour materials.
cards.short_summary: A garden walk connecting the Mission, adobe wall, and campus history.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mission Gardens surround the historic Mission Church and include an adobe wall and the Adobe Lodge, the oldest building on campus.
cards.source_title: What to Expect: de Saisset Museum Tours
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access and any special programming may vary; follow posted campus guidance.

cards.title: See art and California history at de Saisset
cards.subtitle: Adjacent to Mission Santa Clara de Asís
cards.notes: Check the museum’s current visit information, then spend time with the galleries as a focused indoor stop before heading to the next campus landmark.
cards.short_summary: SCU’s on-campus art and history museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The de Saisset Museum stands adjacent to Mission Santa Clara de Asís and is a free museum of art and history.
cards.source_title: About the de Saisset Museum
cards.access_notes: Confirm current gallery hours and exhibition access before visiting.

cards.title: Walk the brick-paved mall
cards.subtitle: From SCU’s main entrance toward the Mission
cards.notes: Use this central walkway to connect the main entrance with the Mission area, pausing to get a feel for the campus layout and mission-style architecture.
cards.short_summary: A central pedestrian route leading to the heart of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Abby Sobrato Mall is a brick-paved route from the University’s main entrance to Mission Santa Clara de Asís.
cards.source_title: SCU Undergraduate Bulletin 2026–27: Campus
cards.access_notes: Outdoor pedestrian route; use normal campus access and safety guidance.

cards.entity_name: Harrington Learning Commons, Sobrato Technology Center, and Orradre Library
cards.title: Choose a first study spot in the Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: SCU University Library
cards.notes: Tour the four levels, then choose a seat, terrace, or study room that fits your plans. Bring your student credentials for any services that require them.
cards.short_summary: A multi-level library for quiet work, collaboration, and technology access.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU’s University Library spans four levels and includes light-filled public spaces, terraces, computers, and study settings.
cards.source_title: Libraries at Santa Clara University
cards.access_notes: Library services, rooms, and hours may have eligibility or reservation requirements.

cards.title: Take the Forge’s self-guided garden tour
cards.subtitle: SCU’s half-acre organic garden
cards.notes: Enter through the front gate and follow the numbered signs at your own pace; stay on paths and tread lightly because this is a working garden.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided look at SCU’s organic teaching garden.
cards.evidence_claim: Forge Garden offers a self-guided tour with numbered stops and is a half-acre edible, organic garden for sustainable food-system education.
cards.source_title: The Forge Garden Self-Guided Tour
cards.access_notes: The garden lists open hours Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–7 p.m., plus events; respect working-garden instructions.

cards.entity_name: Pat Malley Fitness and Recreation Center
cards.title: Get oriented at the Malley Center
cards.subtitle: Campus Recreation facility
cards.notes: Complete any required waiver, bring your ACCESS credential, and choose a low-pressure first activity such as cardio, a court session, or a fitness class.
cards.short_summary: SCU’s student recreation center for fitness and court activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Actively enrolled SCU students receive free access to the Pat Malley Fitness and Recreation Center with a valid ACCESS credential, subject to the annual waiver.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation Memberships
cards.access_notes: Active students need a valid ACCESS credential and annual waiver; check facility schedules before arriving.

cards.title: Plan a swim at Sullivan Aquatic Center
cards.subtitle: Campus Recreation aquatic facility
cards.notes: Check the aquatics schedule before going, then use an available recreation lane for a lap swim or water-walking session with your student access credential.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus pool with recreation lanes when programming permits.
cards.evidence_claim: Current students have free access to the Sullivan Aquatic Center with valid ACCESS credentials, and the center regularly offers lap-swim and water-walking lanes.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation Facility History
cards.access_notes: Lane availability changes when water polo or other groups are scheduled; check the aquatics schedule first.

cards.title: Walk or run by Bellomy Field
cards.subtitle: Campus Recreation outdoor field and track
cards.notes: Use the track for an easy daylight lap or meet a friend nearby, while keeping clear of scheduled intramural games, club practices, and reserved field areas.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor recreation area with a running track around the field.
cards.evidence_claim: Bellomy Field includes a running track that became more consistently accessible after the field’s 2012 renovation.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation Facility History
cards.access_notes: Field availability depends on reservations and games; consult the field schedule before organized use.

cards.entity_name: Paul L. Locatelli, S.J. Student Activity Center
cards.title: Check the Locatelli Center calendar
cards.subtitle: Student Activity Center
cards.notes: Finish by checking what is scheduled in the activity center and noting a future concert, dance, or pre-game gathering that fits your interests and access status.
cards.short_summary: A campus activity venue for gatherings and scheduled events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Paul L. Locatelli, S.J. Student Activity Center has a 6,000-square-foot gathering hall that accommodates dances, concerts, and pre- and post-game activities.
cards.source_title: SCU Undergraduate Bulletin 2026–27: Campus
cards.access_notes: Access depends on the scheduled event; review the relevant organizer’s event details before attending.
